# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b38 — Readable, correctly sized metric tile headings

The Home Environment Manager dashboard sometimes displayed the complete `sensor.badezimmer_...` entity identifier as the title of a small room measurement tile. Long labels could overlap neighboring tiles. This occurred especially when a selected source was unavailable or did not qualify as a supported air-quality metric.

## Fixed in the Lovelace card

- Metric tile headings use the measurement's existing translated name for supported readings.
- When an unavailable/unsupported source has a raw entity ID instead of a friendly label, the card derives a **short human-readable name**. For example `sensor.badezimmer_illumination` becomes **Illumination** (Greek **Φωτισμός**); `sensor.badezimmer_fp300_presence` becomes **Presence** (Greek **Παρουσία**). Common sensor device classes and suffixes are recognized for display only, never to fabricate data or declare the source available.
- Short custom friendly names are preserved; other unknown IDs are shortened to a readable suffix instead of displaying the full namespace and room/device prefix.
- The full source name and exact entity ID remain available on hover via the heading tooltip.
- Headings have a bounded flex layout and **two-line wrap/clamp** inside their own tile. Values and help icons keep their own space; content cannot spill over neighboring metric cards.
- Measurements missing or unsupported by air-quality normalization continue to say **Unavailable**, with no invented reading.

## Scope and validation

Frontend-only change: no modifications to sensor state, Recorder metadata, WebSocket API, physical device commands, selected sources, entity registry or room controls. Beta37's Recorder-safe WebSocket dashboard and all earlier fixes remain present. Canonical integration domain stays `environment_manager`.

CI includes a Node card test for the exact bathroom-like sensor IDs, localized label/tooltip behavior, narrow-tile heading CSS and escaping, plus full Python 3.13/3.14 tests, HA 2026.10, HACS/Hassfest, 38-language catalog assertions and flat HACS extraction.

Stable latest stays v0.5.1.
